sprightly

SPRYTE-lee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sprightly is lively, energetic, and full of spirit.

The sprightly terrier darted circles around dogs half its age at the shelter's adoption event.

Worked Example

The sprightly conductor bounded onto the podium and led the orchestra through the entire symphony without once appearing tired.

Sprightly emphasizes lively, energetic movement -- it's often used to describe someone whose energy is a pleasant surprise.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

lively: Lively means full of energy and enthusiasm, and it fits almost anything — a lively party, a lively debate, a lively child. Sprightly is more particular: it praises a person's light, quick, cheerful energy, often with a note of pleasant surprise about someone older. Everything sprightly is lively, but not the reverse.

spry: Spry means still nimble and quick on your feet, and it is used almost only of older people — a spry grandmother taking the stairs two at a time. Sprightly covers spirit as well as movement and fits any age. Spry praises the body's agility; sprightly praises lively, cheerful energy.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

sluggish: slow-moving and lacking energy

lethargic: lacking energy; unusually drowsy or sluggish

Where it sits · how much energy someone shows — brisk → sprightly → irrepressible

brisk vs. sprightly: Brisk means quick and energetic in a more ordinary way, milder than sprightly.

irrepressible vs. sprightly: Irrepressible means so full of energy that nothing can hold it back, an even more intense liveliness than sprightly.

The pieces

root — spright-

root — spright-: a lively spirit or elf (an old spelling of sprite, from Latin spiritus)

suffix — -ly

suffix — -ly: having the qualities of (Old English -lic)

Put it together

Put it together: Sprightly is built from spright- (an old spelling of sprite, 'a lively spirit or elf,' ultimately from Latin spiritus) + -ly ('having the qualities of') -- literally 'having the qualities of a lively little spirit.'
